proposals: The GST Council should record, in its published minutes, each occasion on which bringing natural gas under GST is considered, with the reasons for deferral, so an industry ask repeated since at least 2021–22 has an official, dated answer rather than silence.

The Department of Revenue should publish an annual estimate of the input tax credit that cannot be claimed because natural gas sits outside GST, so the “stranded tax” FIPI describes is sized by the government rather than asserted by the industry.

The Finance Ministry should publish a list of pre-Budget memoranda received each year, with the submitting body and date, and post the documents themselves, so the link between an industry body’s asks and later Budget changes can be checked independently.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should publish representations it receives from industry associations, such as the March 2024 LPG representation, with its responses, so claims of an “instrumental role” in OALP changes can be verified against the ministry’s own record.

CBIC should maintain a consolidated table of GST rate changes for services, with notification numbers and effective dates, so a change such as exploration, mining and drilling services moving from 12% to 18% can be confirmed from one primary page.
